content: 1. Pentamidine can cause either hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, followed by the opposite effect. Adjustments in insulin dosage and increased glucose monitoring may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended when co-administered with insulin or pentamidine due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. 2. Pentamidine and ioversol both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Pentamidine and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Pentamidine and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Pentamidine increases levels of ivacaftor by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Co-administration of pentamidine with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors requires close monitoring. If unavoidable, monitor for increased QTc interval risk. 8. Pentamidine and ivosidenib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Avoid co-administration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib, or replace with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for increased QTc interval risk. 10. Pentamidine and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Pentamidine decreases levels of L-methylfolate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 12. Pentamidine and lapatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Pentamidine and lefamulin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of lemborexant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 15. Pentamidine and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 16. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Pentamidine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Pentamidine and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Pentamidine and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Pentamidine and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Pentamidine increases levels of lomitapide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 22. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of lonafarnib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce or continue lonafarnib at the starting dose. Lonafarnib may also increase the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Pentamidine and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Pentamidine and macimorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 milliseconds in the corrected QT interval. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 25. Pentamidine and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of mavacamten by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 27. Pentamidine and mavorixafor both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 28. Pentamidine decreases the effects of metformin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Pentamidine and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Pentamidine and methoxyflurane both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of midazolam intranasal by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may cause higher midazolam systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 32. Pentamidine and mifepristone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 33. Pentamidine and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Pentamidine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Pentamidine and neomycin PO both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Pentamidine and nilotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Pentamidine and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Pentamidine and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Pentamidine and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Pentamidine and olanzapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 41. Pentamidine and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the effects of beta-2 agonists on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 42. Pentamidine and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid use in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant medications that prolong the QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 43. Pentamidine and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Pentamidine and oxaliplatin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Oxaliplatin will also increase the level or effect of pentamidine. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Pentamidine and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 46. Pentamidine and paliperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 47. Pentamidine and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval, and its prescribing information states that use with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. 48. Pentamidine and paromomycin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The clinical significance is unknown. 49. Pentamidine and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Pentamidine and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Pentamidine and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Pentamidine increases levels of peramivir by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution when peramivir is co-administered with nephrotoxic drugs. 53. Pentamidine and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 54. Pentamidine and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 55. Pentamidine and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 56. Pentamidine and polymyxin B both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Pentamidine and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 58. Pentamidine and potassium citrate/citric acid both increase serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Pentamidine and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 60. Pentamidine and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 61. Pentamidine and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 62. Pentamidine and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 63. Pentamidine and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 64. Pentamidine and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 65. Pentamidine and quetiapine both increase the toxicity of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. 66. Pentamidine and quinidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 67. Pentamidine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Pentamidine and quizartinib both increase the effects of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 69. Pentamidine and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 70. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 71. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used with caution when co-administered with a drug with a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 72. Pentamidine and risperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 73. Pentamidine and romidepsin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 74. Rucaparib increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP2C19 substrates if clinically indicated. 75. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of ruxolitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 76. Pentamidine and selpercatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Pentamidine and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 78. Pentamidine and sevoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 79. Pentamidine and siponimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 80. Pentamidine decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 81. Pentamidine and solifenacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 82. Pentamidine and sorafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Pentamidine and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 84. Sparsentan increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Sparsentan (a CYP2C19 inducer) decreases exposure of CYP2C19 substrates and reduces efficacy related to these substrates. 85. Stiripentol increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions are experienced when administered concomitantly with stiripentol. 86. Pentamidine and streptomycin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The clinical significance is unknown. 87. Pentamidine and streptozocin both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 88. Pentamidine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
